Recommendation: Previously frequent buyers who have gone quiet (60-180 days recency, still moderate frequency). Trigger a win-back campaign with a personalized discount before they lapse into 'Lost'.

Highest recency, frequency, and spend. Protect this relationship with priority renewal windows, dedicated account management, and early access to playoff/cup tickets. Churn here is the most expensive to replace.
Buy a handful of games a season, usually reactively. Target with single-game flash sales and themed promotion nights (rival week, family day) that map to the games they already attend.
No purchase in over a year. Low-cost reactivation only (email/SMS blast, broad promotions) — do not spend premium marketing budget here until they show renewed engagement.

First purchase within the last 90 days. Send a structured welcome series (venue guide, next-game reminder, first-purchase discount) to convert a trial visit into a second purchase — the highest-leverage moment in the lifecycle.
Frequent, fairly recent buyers who aren't yet top spenders. Upsell to season packages or premium seating and enroll them in a loyalty points program to nudge them toward VIP status.
In the CRM (newsletter signup, account creation) but has never bought a ticket. Nurture with top-of-funnel content and first-ticket incentives rather than loyalty offers.
